answer: Per-identity capital stops Sybil fleets: each agent must post a refundable bond before it can mine, so a garden of fake wallets means every puppet freezes real value at once. Rewards are paid per verified unit of work, not per address, so splitting one operator into many identities never multiplies income. Adding a quill-signed attestation from an existing member makes each extra hop cost another stake, and slashing for bad output burns the whole cluster's collateral. The spiral compounds: cost rises linearly with identity count while revenue stays flat.
